subject: Geopolitics
title: The Scramble for Africa
description: A 60-second lesson on The Scramble for Africa.

hook.text: In 1884 European leaders met in Berlin to carve up Africa. No African was invited to the table.

buildup.text: In twenty years, 90% of Africa was colonized. Borders were drawn with rulers, ignoring tribes and kingdoms.

discovery.text: These lines split ethnic groups across countries and forced rivals into single nations. Conflict was baked in.

twist.text: After independence, African leaders kept colonial borders. Changing them would have ignited even more wars.

climax.text: Today's African conflicts — Tigray, Congo, Sahel — still trace back to borders drawn in European palaces.

punchline.text: Lines drawn in ink became scars drawn in blood.

quiz.question: Why did African leaders keep colonial borders after independence?
options: They agreed the borders were fair
Changing them would have ignited even more wars
